name: Populism
summary: Populism, in the leading scholarly definition, is a thin-centred ideology that divides society into the pure people and a corrupt elite and says politics should express the people's general will. It has little program of its own and attaches to host ideologies, usually socialism on the left and nationalism on the right. It favors direct popular decision-making and distrusts institutions that check the majority.
scope: The ideational core as defined by Cas Mudde and Cristobal Rovira Kaltwasser, plus the historical US People's Party (Omaha Platform, 1892) as a primary example. Economic, immigration and cultural answers are mostly left neutral because they come from host ideologies; right-wing and left-wing variants are noted where they differ. Excludes the economic-mismanagement and purely rhetorical-style uses of the term.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred: the Omaha Platform demands more popular control of the ballot and government, not less.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: No stated position; the answer comes from the host ideology.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: No stated position; the answer comes from the host ideology (nationalist variants might hold land, civic variants not).

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Populism takes its answer from its host ideology and has no stated position on discrimination by private owners.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Set by the host ideology; adherents are split; the sources do not address it and the answer is not inferred from any stated principle.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Set by the host ideology; adherents are split; the sources do not address it and the answer is not inferred from any stated principle.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred from distrust of an unelected elite and the call for popular rather than expert choice of rulers.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; right and left hosts differ.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The Omaha Platform says alien ownership of land should be prohibited and lands held by aliens reclaimed; right-wing populism shares the nationalism.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Left populism may accept it and right-wing populism rejects it; the ideational core is silent.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position on consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Thin-centred ideology with no stated position; hosts differ.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Right populists restrict foreign funding while left populists do not; the thin core takes no position.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Populism takes no position here; right populists favor it, left populists mostly do not.

residents-only-property.rationale: The thin ideology does not address it; the answer comes from the host ideology.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Populists mostly take no position and many right variants defend marriage; inferred from host ideologies.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Populists want government answerable to the people against a secretive elite, which suggests openness. Inferred.

local-production.rationale: The thin core does not address it; the answer comes from the host ideology.
